title: Teacher-student relationship and teaching styles in primary education. A model of analysis.
venue: Journal of Professional Capital and Community
extended_summary:
This paper examines how students perceive the relationship with their teachers in primary education and how those perceptions are associated with two teaching styles: directive and participative. The authors address a gap in the literature by studying the interaction between teaching style and teacher-student relationship from the student’s point of view, rather than relying on teacher reports or direct classroom observation.

The study uses a structural equation model built from existing questionnaire data from the 2018/2019 Diagnostic Assessment in the Canary Islands, Spain. The sample includes 21,126 sixth-grade primary students from 623 schools. The authors construct latent variables for directive teaching style, participative teaching style, emotional relationship, and educational relationship from student questionnaire items, and then test whether the relationships between these constructs differ by student characteristics such as gender, quarter of birth, and parents’ educational level.

The main findings are that participative teaching style is more strongly associated with positive perceived teacher-student relationships than directive teaching style. Directive style is more tied to the educational relationship, while participative style is more tied to the emotional relationship. The study also finds heterogeneity in student perceptions: girls report more participative teaching and more positive emotional and educational relationships than boys, while students from lower parental educational backgrounds tend to perceive directive teaching more clearly and, in some cases, report stronger educational relationships. The paper concludes that student feedback is useful for understanding classroom practice, but interpretation must account for differences in student background.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed correlational study using structural equation modeling and mean-comparison tests on census data, not an experimental design. It provides moderate methodological rigor for association testing, but it cannot establish causal effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports statistically significant but non-causal associations and no intervention effect sizes in the K-12 sense. Its practical impact is mainly conceptual and measurement-focused, with potential usefulness for policy and school diagnostics rather than demonstrated outcome gains.

finding.finding_summary: Using census data from 21,126 sixth-grade students in the Canary Islands, the study found that perceived teaching style is strongly associated with students’ perceptions of teacher-student relationship. Participative teaching style correlated more with both emotional and educational relationship than directive style (all coefficients significant at 1%), but these are correlational SEM results rather than causal effects.
finding.measure: Structural equation model of student questionnaire latent constructs: directive teaching style, participative teaching style, emotional relationship, educational relationship

finding.finding_summary: The paper’s main contribution is a replicable measurement model for student feedback on teaching styles and teacher-student relationship, with potential use in periodic diagnostic assessments and cross-context educational policy analysis. It argues the model could support context-specific policy proposals, but this is proposed utility rather than observed institutional impact.
finding.measure: Proposed SEM-based model for diagnostic assessment / student feedback use
